title: The 5 Deepest Mines Ever Dug, Ranked (All 5 Are in One Country)

scenes.text: The five deepest mines humans have ever dug. All five are in one country.

scenes.label: Driefontein · 3.42 km
scenes.text: Number five: Driefontein, South Africa, 3.42 kilometres down. A gold mine, and still working today.

scenes.label: East Rand · 3.59 km
scenes.text: Number four: East Rand Mine, South Africa, 3.585 kilometres. Closed in 2008.

scenes.label: Savuka · 3.7 km
scenes.text: Number three: Savuka, 3.7 kilometres straight down, in the same South African gold field as number two.

scenes.label: TauTona · 3.9 km
scenes.text: Number two: TauTona, 3.9 kilometres deep, with around 800 kilometres of tunnels under one mine.

scenes.label: Mponeng · 4.0 km
scenes.text: Number one: Mponeng, 4 kilometres below the surface, the deepest mine on Earth. Top to bottom takes just over an hour. And it's still digging.

description:
The five deepest mines ever dug, ranked by depth below the surface. All five are South African gold mines.
Mponeng reaches 4.0 km and the trip to the bottom takes just over an hour; TauTona reaches 3.9 km with around 800 km of tunnels; Savuka 3.7 km; East Rand Mine 3.585 km (closed 2008); Driefontein 3.42 km.
Would you ride the cage 4 kilometres down?
first_comment: Four kilometres down is about nine Empire State Buildings stacked underground. Which would you put at number one, and what should we rank next?
